about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I am a Computer Vision and Applied Machine Learning Engineer based in Shizuoka, Japan, with hands-on experience spanning mobility AI research, industrial robotics software, and scalable cloud web services.

Currently, I develop mobility-related AI and visual understanding systems at Toyota Motor Corporation's Higashi-Fuji Research Center through BREXA Technology—turning experimental models into reproducible internal software and patent-disclosure concepts.

Previously, I developed C++ control software for surface-mount robotics at Yamaha Motor Robotics (via Aspark) and built cloud game-server infrastructure serving 130,000+ users at Cloud Creative Studios in Kyoto.

items.fullCompany: BREXA Technology, Inc. (assigned to Toyota Motor Corporation)
items.overview: Developing AI and camera-understanding systems for next-generation mobility research at Toyota's Higashi-Fuji Research Center.
items.impact: Improved road-flood detection accuracy from 76% to 98% and submitted a concept through Toyota's internal patent disclosure process.
bullets: Project 1 — Flooded-Road Detection: Built an AI pipeline using ~2,000 vehicle-camera images, synthetic data, ResNet, YOLOP, and segmentation so vehicles can detect flooded roads even in low light, reflections, and low resolution.
Project 2 — Driving-Video Data Analysis: Compared rule-based, unsupervised learning, and LLM-based methods to automatically analyze and summarize driving-video annotations.
Project 3 — Video Analysis & Annotation Automation: Built internal tools for object detection, tracking, OCR text extraction, and map-matching support to speed up research workflows.
Authored reproducible technical documentation and presented findings in Japanese for Toyota's internal IP disclosure process.

items.fullCompany: Aspark Co., Ltd. (assigned to Yamaha Motor Robotics Co., Ltd.)
items.overview: Developed control software for Yamaha's high-speed Surface-Mount Technology (SMT) robotics machines (YRM10, YRM20, YRM20DL) used in electronics manufacturing.
items.impact: Delivered reliable C++ features and workflow optimizations in a 16-member Japanese engineering team.
bullets: What I built: Added new machine features, refactored legacy C++ code, and fixed production software defects on Windows.
How it helped: Improved machine control workflows to support factory tact-time (speed) and operational stability.
Collaboration: Worked directly with Yamaha engineers in Japanese on detailed design specs, SQL data handling, testing, and code reviews.

items.overview: Built a cloud-based game-server management platform and live-ops web portal serving 130,000+ active players.
items.impact: Planned, built, and deployed end-to-end backend APIs, admin UI, and automated Azure cloud backups.
bullets: What I built: Backend services in C# / ASP.NET and responsive web management dashboards in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap.
Core features: Engineered user authentication, in-game gacha/shop/event systems, and real-time KPI analytics on Azure, Cosmos DB, and Redis.
Reliability: Automated CI/CD builds with GitHub Actions and designed scheduled KPI data-processing and backup pipelines.
